column3: Open a command prompt, validate the active .NET SDK and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App runtime versions via dotnet --info, create a solution + global.json (validating it pins the SDK version), then dynamically loop over every installed Microsoft.AspNetCore.App major version (collected at run time from dotnet --list-runtimes, so 8/9/10/11/... all work) building & self-contained-publishing a console app, opening its .deps.json in Visual Studio, and validating the runtime version band. MyGlobal is left on disk after the run.

column4: Trigger
Resolve the current user's home directory (works on any drive).
Remove leftover MyGlobal/test folders and temp files from any previous run.
column6: ["cmd.exe","--cwd","{vars.home}","--args","/c","rmdir /s /q MyGlobal & rmdir /s /q test & del /q dn_info.txt aspnet_majors.json"]

column4: Collect installed AspNetCore.App major versions and the active SDK version.
column16: Major versions and SDK version collected.

column4: Auto-detect the installed Visual Studio devenv.exe (edition/version agnostic).
Launch cmd.exe in the home dir with a unique window title.
Bring the command prompt to the foreground.
Run dotnet --info into a file and echo it to screen.
Submit the command.
Capture the dotnet --info output.
Assert the active SDK version is present in the captured output.
Assert the AspNetCore.App runtime is present.
Create a new solution in MyGlobal.
Submit.
Change into MyGlobal.
Submit.
Create global.json (pins the running SDK version).
Submit.
Open global.json in Notepad.
Submit.
Locate the Notepad window (matched by filename; avoids the GDI helper).
Screenshot the global.json contents.
Assert global.json pins the active SDK version.
column16: global.json version matches the SDK version.

column4: Close Notepad.
Yield the next collected AspNetCore.App major version (loops once per installed version).
Open a new command prompt for this version.
Bring it to the foreground.
Make the test directory (may already exist; harmless).
Submit.
Change into test.
Submit.
Create the console app for this version.
Submit.
Change into the project directory.
Submit.
Publish self-contained for win-x86 and echo the result.
Submit (publish runs; then prints the result).
Capture the publish result.
Assert the publish produced the project output (build succeeded).
Open the deps.json in Visual Studio.
column17: Visual Studio opens the deps file.

column4: Bring Visual Studio to the foreground.
Screenshot the deps file in Visual Studio.
Assert the deps file references this runtime version band.
column17: Deps version matches this AspNetCore.App major.

column4: Close Visual Studio.
Close this version's command prompt.
Close the original command prompt (MyGlobal is left on disk).
column16: Original command prompt closed; MyGlobal preserved.
